title: Outcome check
description: Reads the real end state after a trial (a database row, a file, an HTTP resource, a page) and compares it to what should be there. Without `read` the state is `trial.state`, the snapshot the agent's own script wrote into trial.json. With `read` the runner reads the state itself, so the agent's script cannot report a state that is not there.

backend.description: What kind of state this is. It selects the reader when `read` is set; page has no reader and always uses trial.state.

read.description: How the runner reads the state after the trial. sql: `file` and `queries`. fs: `file` or `exists`. http: `url`. Paths are relative to the trial directory and may not leave it. `validate --deep` and `run --dry-run` have no trial directory, so there the check is compared against the reference solution's `state`.

file.description: sql: a SQLite file in the trial directory, opened read-only. fs: a JSON file in the trial directory; the parsed JSON is the state.

queries.description: sql: one SELECT per `expect` key. The first column of the first row is the value; no row is null.

exists.description: fs: paths to test. The state is { exists: [true, false, ...] } in the same order, so expect exists[0]: true.

url.description: http: the resource to fetch; the JSON response is the state. {trial_dir}, {task} and {trial} are filled, and ${NAME} takes an environment variable. A network failure or a 5xx is an infra error, not a failed check; a 4xx gives the state { http_status }.

headers.description: http: request headers; ${NAME} takes an environment variable, so a token never sits in the task file.

expect.description: Dotted path to a value in the state, e.g. refunds.status: processed, or rows[0].id. Every entry must match.
